rows.description: I keep it secret because I fear being mocked, which lets the scammer's damage grow. Wise: speaking up early can recover money and stops the loop. Harmful: silence, which scammers rely on.

rows.description: A friend forwards a "guaranteed profit" scheme he believes in. He is not evil, just caught. Wise: check the source before spreading it, question calmly, and keep the friendship while refusing the scheme.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, deceit, humiliation, shame

rows.description: I am furious and want to trap the fraudster myself. Wise: give what I have to the police and cyber cell; do not chase him alone, as that risks more loss or danger. Harmful: revenge fantasies that lead to further scams.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, humiliation, shame, trust

rows.description: My parent scolds me: "How could you fall for this?" I feel doubly hurt. Wise: hear the fear behind it, ask for help on the next steps, and offer to teach them scam signs too. Harmful: blaming back.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: deceit, humiliation, shame, trust

rows.description: A finance influencer shows luxury cars and says his course changed his life. I feel drawn in. Wise: ask how he actually earns, check registration and track record. Harmful: buying a dream instead of evidence.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, manipulation, obsession, shame, trust

rows.description: Countdown timers, "only 5 seats" and screenshots of profits push me to hurry. Wise: urgency is a sales tool; slow down, read the risks, and never invest money I cannot afford to lose.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, obsession, shame, trust

rows.description: My friend doubled money on a hot tip, and I feel left behind. Wise: survivor stories hide the losers; learn basics like index funds, diversification and time. Harmful: chasing his win with borrowed money.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, manipulation, obsession, shame, trust

rows.description: I check the trading app every few minutes and my mood follows the chart. Wise: notice it is closer to a gambling loop than planning; set limits and turn off notifications. Harmful: doubling down to recover losses.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, manipulation, shame, trust

rows.description: Friends want me to join a pooled scheme because I am the one who "understands markets". I feel flattered and burdened. Wise: be honest about my limits and do not take others' money or promise returns.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, manipulation, obsession, shame

rows.description: I lost most of my savings on a tip and feel foolish. Wise: accept the cost, stop trying to win it back, write the lesson, and rebuild slowly. Harmful: another risky bet to erase the loss.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, manipulation, obsession, trust
